pull.title: test: optionally run functional tests via CTest
pull.body:
Expose individual functional tests through the same CTest interface used for unit tests, making them easier to select, inspect, and rerun from the command line or CTest-aware IDEs.

Scheduling unit and functional tests together may improve parallel execution. It also enables per-test results and timings to be uploaded to our [Bitcoin Core CDash instance](https://my.cdash.org/index.php?project=bitcoin-core), helping track failures and runtime changes across builds.

Registration is opt-in with `BUILD_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS=ON` and requires CMake 4.4 or newer. The existing runner remains available for RPC coverage and CSV results. The native macOS CI job exercises the combined CTest workflow and passes. See `test/README.md` for usage and limitations.

build: optionally register functional tests with CTest

Native discovery makes functional cases available to CTest scheduling,
filters and dashboards alongside unit tests. Require CMake 4.4 only when
this optional registration is enabled, avoiding a second discovery
implementation while retaining the existing minimum for normal builds.

Use fixtures to prepare the shared chain cache before parallel execution.
Run cache creation through the same Python wrapper as the test cases so
its timeout and failure handling cannot drift from theirs.

Run unit and functional cases together in one native CI job to keep the
optional CTest path exercised.

running them twice.

test: avoid CTest temporary directory collisions

Concurrent variants of the same script can observe the same wall-clock value
on macOS and select an identical temporary directory. The second test then
fails before framework setup completes.

Use a random UUID suffix so directory names do not depend on clock resolution.
Leave directory creation and cleanup with the test framework to preserve
failed logs and its requirement that the supplied path does not exist.

comments.body:
Not quite, although it was incorrect (thanks!)

(somethign like this) is needed because native/upstream `discover_tests()` preserves the empty `\5` replacement for tests without an optional argument. Without filtering it, `--ctest-direct` sees the script plus an empty second “test” and rejects the invocation.

The explicit `--` separator is needed separately because `argparse` allows option abbreviation by default: CTest’s child option `--tmpdir` (tdestined for test_framework.py) can otherwise be consumed as the runner’s `--tmpdirprefix` option instead of being forwarded. The `arg != "--"` filter removes that separator before invoking the child test.

(in fact, I think this is a seperate bug and we could disable argparse [allow_abbrev](https://docs.python.org/3/library/argparse.html#allow-abbrev) to fix it properly. Or perhaps makes better sense to fix that first, before these changes...)

comments.body: added a short comment documenting the source-tree resolution (and dropped `PYTHON_GIL=1` which is set by _test/CMakeLists.txt_ on each test already.

not sure about exposing this in CI.  This will silently ignore `TEST_RUNNER_EXTRA`, and having two ways to achieve the same seems confusing anyway. 

However, not exposing it in CI will also make it less useful ...

Thank you for taking a look, and fair point!

I don't consider these strict duplicates: `CTEST_TESTS` is a coarse CTest label selection: all, functional, or nonfunctional whereas `TEST_RUNNER_EXTRA` contains runner-specific behavior and test arguments.

However they do certainly overlap, and I think (for now) I will amend the commit to fail if `TEST_RUNNER_EXTRA` is non-empty in `CTEST` mode as a check on silently doing something else than the tests might have indented.

Longer-term, say we switch all tests over to ctest, I would see us dropping `RUN_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS_WITH_CTEST` (it would be default/on for all and unneeded), probably alos remove `CTEST_TESTS` and instead have each job just construct its own ctest command directly, and maybe even remove `TEST_RUNNER_EXTRA` (depening on whether we can get all supported options ported to ctest).

Why would porting be hard? The leftover from "${TEST_RUNNER_EXTRA[@]}" would just end up in `passon_args` and be exported to the test list, no?


This pull is adding 500 LOC of logic complexity, so my preference would be to at least keep the overhead low.

Recall the alternative to this would be to write it in a few trivial lines of Python (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/32770#issuecomment-3714857697)
Also, recall that Python would work when testing win64-cross builds, but CTest does not.
